lines.japanese: 地元の駅へ戻った頃には、太陽は沈む寸前だった。
lines.english: By the time we returned to my local station, the sun was on the verge of setting.

lines.japanese: 地上に漏れている光は群青色に浸食され、ほとんど紫がかっている。東の空には星が見える。
lines.english: Ultramarine was consuming the light that remained over the earth, turning it almost violet. Stars had appeared in the eastern sky.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君の家ってこっち？」
lines.english: “Is your house this way?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 二階建ての煙草屋の前を通りすぎつつ、僕はその先の瓦の屋根を指差した。
lines.english: As we passed a two-story tobacco shop, I pointed toward the tiled roof beyond it.

lines.japanese: 本当は山科さんに「ここでいいよ」と言いたかったけど、とうとう家に着くまでその言葉は出てこなかった。
lines.english: I had meant to tell Yamashina, “This is far enough,” but the words never came before we reached the house.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、ここでいい？」
lines.english: “Will you be all right from here?”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫だよ」
lines.english: “I'll be fine.”

lines.japanese: ブロック塀の前で僕はうなずいた。当然のことだけど、家の明かりは点いていなかった。
lines.english: I nodded before the concrete-block wall. Naturally, there were no lights on inside.

lines.japanese: 「家族のひとは遅いの？」
lines.english: “Will your family be home late?”

lines.japanese: 沈みかけた太陽を見ながらの山科さんに訊ねられた。僕はもう一度うなずく。
lines.english: She asked as she watched the sinking sun. I nodded once more.

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫……大丈夫だから」
lines.english: “It’s all right... I’ll be all right.”

lines.japanese: 「鍵は？」
lines.english: “Your key?”

lines.japanese: 「鍵……ああ、そうか……鍵がないと……ドアは開かないもんね……」
lines.english: “My key... Oh. Of course... The door won’t open without it...”

lines.japanese: ポケットを探ってみたけど鍵はない。慌ててリュックを肩から外して脇のポケットを探る。
lines.english: I searched my pockets, but the key was not there. In alarm I slipped the backpack from my shoulders and rummaged through its side pocket.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あった……はは、そりゃないと入れないもんね……じゃあ、はい……」
lines.english: “Ah, here it is... Ha ha. I couldn’t get inside without it... Here...”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あれっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: なにをやっているんだろう。僕は山科さんに鍵を差しだしていた。こんなものを渡されたら、彼女じゃなくても不思議そうな顔になるだろう。
lines.english: What was I doing? I was holding the key out to Yamashina. Anyone, not only her, would have looked puzzled to be handed such a thing.

lines.japanese: 「ご、ごめん、何してるんだろう、おれ」
lines.english: “S-sorry. What am I doing?”

lines.japanese: 「ここでいいよ。ありがとう」
lines.english: “This is far enough. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「よくないって」
lines.english: “No, it isn’t.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は僕の差しだした鍵を受けとると、年季の入ったブロック塀の中へと入っていった。
lines.english: She accepted the key I held out and passed through the opening in the weathered block wall.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれっ？」
lines.english: “W-wait?”

lines.japanese: 「おじゃまするね」
lines.english: “Excuse me for intruding.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは右手で玄関のドアに鍵を差しこむと、かちゃんと音がしたのを確認してから僕を手招きした。
lines.english: Yamashina inserted the key into the front door with her right hand. When the lock clicked, she beckoned me forward.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ええと……あれ？」
lines.english: “Um... What?”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、自分じゃ気がついてないのかもしれないけど、まだ顔色悪いよ」
lines.english: “You may not realize it yourself, Haneda, but you still look pale.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことないよ」
lines.english: “Th-that's not true.”

lines.japanese: 「だから気がついてないんだってば」
lines.english: “That’s why I said you haven’t realized it.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは片側の髪を掻きあげながら、さっきマンションで会ったときみたいに僕の袖の端をつかんでくいくいと引っ張る。
lines.english: Brushing up the hair on one side of her face, Yamashina caught the edge of my sleeve and gave it several small tugs, just as she had outside the apartment building.

lines.japanese: 「えと、おじゃまします」
lines.english: “Um... Excuse me for intruding.”

lines.japanese: なんだか他人の家みたいに思えたから、僕は頭を下げながら敷居をまたいだ。
lines.english: The house somehow felt as though it belonged to somebody else, and I bowed as I stepped across the threshold.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、ノスタルジー……」
lines.english: “Oh... Nostalgia.”

lines.japanese: 家の中に入ると、山科さんはそんな感想を述べた。うーん、外観は叔母さんが旧形態なことを気にしているけど、中もやっぱりそんな感じなのかな。
lines.english: That was Yamashina’s verdict once we were inside. My aunt worried that the outside looked old-fashioned, but perhaps the interior had the same quality.

lines.japanese: 僕は他のひとの家に入ったことがほとんどないから、一戸建ての平均より古いのかよく分からない。でも山科さんに言われると、少しだけ叔母さんがご近所を気にしている理由が分かる気がした。
lines.english: I had entered so few other people’s houses that I could not judge whether ours was older than the average detached home. Hearing Yamashina say it, however, I began to understand why my aunt cared what the neighbors thought.

lines.japanese: おまけに彼女が階段を上るとき、小さいけれど軋む音がした。うーん古い家だと思われないといいなあ。
lines.english: The stairs even gave a small creak beneath her feet as she climbed. Mmm. I hoped she would not decide it was a terribly old house.

lines.japanese: ん？　階段？　山科さんはどこに向かってるんだろう……。
lines.english: Hm? The stairs? Where was Yamashina going...?

lines.japanese: 「羽田君の部屋、どっち？」
lines.english: “Which one is your room?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 部屋……僕の部屋に来るってことか？
lines.english: My room... She meant to come into my room?

lines.japanese: 「なにか悩んでるんでしょ？　話聞くよ」
lines.english: “Something is troubling you, isn’t it? I’ll listen.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんが優しい顔で微笑む。僕は悩んでるように見えるのかな。
lines.english: Yamashina smiled gently. Did I look troubled?

lines.japanese: だけど、山科さんが話を聞いてくれるって言ってるんだから、思ってることを全部話してみるのもいいのかもしれない。
lines.english: Still, if Yamashina offered to listen, perhaps I could tell her everything on my mind.

lines.japanese: それに今は、なんだかひとと話したい気分だ。
lines.english: Besides, just then I wanted very much to speak to another person.

lines.japanese: 僕は彼女の前を通りすぎると、自分の部屋の引き戸を開けた。
lines.english: I passed her and slid open the door to my room.

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃい」
lines.english: “Welcome.”

lines.japanese: 僕の部屋にはもともと物が少ない。それは幸いだった。
lines.english: My room had never contained many things. That much was fortunate.

lines.japanese: だけど散らかってることは否めない。普段から掃除の習慣をつけておけばよかった。僕は少なからず、自分の不精を反省した。
lines.english: I could not deny that those few things lay in disarray. I should have made a habit of cleaning regularly. I felt more than a little remorse for my slovenliness.

lines.japanese: 「おじゃまします……」
lines.english: “Excuse me...”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは家に入ったときよりも、控えめなおじゃましますを口にした。彼女の視線がまず止まったのは、机の横に置いてあるパソコンだ。
lines.english: Yamashina said it more diffidently than she had upon entering the house. The first thing to arrest her gaze was the computer beside my desk.

lines.japanese: つつつと絨毯の上に足を滑らせて、パソコンに手を伸ばす。
lines.english: She slid across the carpet in tiny steps and reached toward it.

lines.japanese: 「この子がいつも繋いでくれてるんだあ」
lines.english: “So this is the little one that always connects us.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんがケースの縁を右手で撫でてる。まるで生き物を撫でるような手つきだ。
lines.english: Yamashina stroked the rim of the case with her right hand, caressing it almost as though it were alive.

lines.japanese: ただ、ドライブの中に女の子の絵が描いてあるＤＶＤが入ってるから、あまり近づいてほしくないのが本音だ。
lines.english: The truth was, a DVD decorated with a picture of a girl was still in the drive, and I would rather she did not inspect it too closely.

lines.japanese: 「そんなに珍しいかなあ」
lines.english: “Is it so unusual?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、うん、へええ……」
lines.english: “Oh... Yes. Wow...”

lines.japanese: 僕の質問に対する返事は、感動詞の間に挟まれた。もしかして山科さんって、パソコンオタクだったりするのかな。
lines.english: Her answer to my question came buried among interjections. Could Yamashina perhaps be a computer enthusiast?

lines.japanese: 「あの、話……いいのかな」
lines.english: “Um... What about our talk?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は背中を向けたまま返事をすると、パソコンの前に小さく、手を揃えて正座した。どうしてそんな隅っこに行くんだろう。
lines.english: Still facing away, she answered and knelt formally before the computer, making herself small, her hands folded neatly together. Why had she gone to such a remote corner?

lines.japanese: 「あの、これ使ったらどうかな」
lines.english: “Um... Why don’t you use this?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 僕は脇にある座布団を指し示した。彼女はそれを足の下に敷かず、膝の上に乗せた。
lines.english: I indicated a cushion nearby. Rather than place it beneath her legs, she settled it across her lap.

lines.japanese: 「座布団は床に敷いて使うものだよ」
lines.english: “You’re supposed to put a cushion on the floor and sit on it.”

lines.japanese: 「ん……いい、このままの方が落ちつくから」
lines.english: “Mmm... No. I feel calmer this way.”

lines.japanese: 小さな手が、膝に乗せている座布団をぎゅっと握る。僕は正座している彼女の前に、片膝を立てながら腰を下ろした。
lines.english: Her small hands clutched the cushion in her lap. I sat before her with one knee raised.

lines.japanese: 「え、そうすると落ちつくの？」
lines.english: “Holding something like that calms you?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、なにか抱いてると安心するかな」
lines.english: “Yes. I think I feel safer when I’m hugging something.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、居心地悪いのかな」
lines.english: “Mmm. Do you feel uncomfortable here?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうじゃないよ」
lines.english: “Oh, no. That's not it.”

lines.japanese: 「男の子の部屋に初めて入るからなんだか恐縮しちゃって。それだけなのに、不思議だね」
lines.english: “I’ve never been in a boy’s room before, so I suddenly feel terribly self-conscious. That’s all, but... strange, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 改めて見ると、山科さんの顔はいつも以上に前髪で隠れていた。
lines.english: Looking again, I saw that Yamashina’s face was hidden behind her bangs even more than usual.

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは前に付きあっていたひとの部屋には行ったことがないんだ。ちょっと距離が離れてたところに住んでたのかな。
lines.english: So she had never visited the room of the person she used to date. Perhaps they had lived some distance away.

lines.japanese: 「それで、大罪とか、聖騎士とか？」
lines.english: “Now, then. Something about a mortal sin and being a holy knight?”

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: そうだ、さっき僕は山科さんの前で、迂闊な発言をしてしまった。そんなことを口走って周りのひとに避けられたのは、何度も経験したことなのに。
lines.english: That was right. I had spoken carelessly in front of Yamashina, even though blurting out things like that had made people avoid me time and again.

lines.japanese: 「ええと、おれそんなこと言ったっけ」
lines.english: “Um... Did I say something like that?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、居場所がないとか、許されないとか」
lines.english: “Yes. You said there was nowhere you belonged and that you were no longer allowed back.”

lines.japanese: 「私なら何でも聞いてあげられると思うから、言ってみて？」
lines.english: “I think I can listen to anything you need to tell me. Won’t you try telling me?”

lines.japanese: 「いや冗談だよ。そんなの、本気で言うはずがないよ」
lines.english: “It was only a joke. I couldn’t possibly have meant any of that.”

lines.japanese: 「言うよ。言ったから話を聞きにきたんだよ」
lines.english: “You could. You said it, and that’s why I came to listen.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、それは想像の話で」
lines.english: “But it was only something I imagined.”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君」
lines.english: “Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんの瞳が優しく僕を貫く。
lines.english: Yamashina’s gentle eyes pierced straight through me.

lines.japanese: 「先に突きやぶってきたのは羽田君――」
lines.english: “You were the one who broke through first—”

lines.japanese: 「……だったと思うよ」
lines.english: “...or at least, I think you were.”

lines.japanese: そして少し困ったように、でも楽しそうに微笑んだ。
lines.english: Then she smiled, looking a little troubled but pleased all the same.

lines.japanese: 「そっか……」
lines.english: “I see...”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうだね」
lines.english: “Yes. You're right.”

lines.japanese: 「これは“たとえば”の話だけど。」
lines.english: “This is only a ‘what if’ story.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんに話したことで気が緩んでいたんだろうか。
lines.english: Perhaps telling Watarai had loosened something inside me.

lines.japanese: 僕は今日、今まで誰にもしてこなかった話を二人のひとに話した。
lines.english: Today, I told two people a story I had never told anyone before.
